chunks: And by his chain of narration, from Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
to Ali: Give glad tidings to your followers, for I will be their intercessor on the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which nothing will benefit them except my intercession.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's intercession for his followers on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instructs Ali (peace be upon him) to convey the glad tidings of exclusive intercession (*Shafa'ah*) to his followers, emphasizing that on the Day of Resurrection, no other means of salvation will suffice. This highlights the central Shia doctrine of the Prophet's unique role as the intercessor for the *Shi'a*, linking the community's identity directly to the Prophet's authority and mercy. The narration underscores that while intercession is a divine permission, its efficacy is specifically tied to the Prophet's relationship with his devoted followers.
